body.en: A *Karnaugh* map has one cell per row of the truth table: 4 cells for 2 variables, 8 for 3, 16 for 4. Rows and columns are labelled in Gray-code order (00, 01, 11, 10), so cells that touch, including across opposite edges, differ in exactly one variable. Enter a 1 in each cell whose minterm is in the function. For four variables with rows AB and columns CD, the cell numbers are 0 1 3 2 / 4 5 7 6 / 12 13 15 14 / 8 9 11 10.

title.en: Reading the result, and POS from 0s

body.en: Every 1 must be in at least one group. Start with 1s that can be grouped in only one way, then use the largest groups for the rest; a group whose 1s are all already covered is redundant. Each group gives a product term and the terms are ORed: the reduced SOP. Grouping the 0s instead gives the reduced POS: each group of 0s gives a sum term with each unchanging variable complemented if it is 1, and the terms are ANDed. Don't-care cells (X) may be used as 1s or 0s to make bigger groups.

points.en: Don't-cares may be included when helpful

explanation.en: Keep only the variables that stay the same across the group: the row AB = 01 fixes A'B; cells 0 and 2 differ only in C; rows 01 and 11 share only B = 1; a single cell keeps all four variables.

problem.en: Minimise F(A, B, C, D) = Σ(0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 13, 15) using a K-map.

steps.en: Row AB = 00 has 1s in all four cells (0, 1, 3, 2): quad A'B'.
Column CD = 01 and 11 in rows AB = 01 and 11 (5, 7, 13, 15): quad BD.
Cells 1, 3, 5, 7 also form a quad A'D, but 1 and 3 are covered by A'B' and 5 and 7 by BD, so it is redundant.

narration.en: Minimise F(A, B, C, D) = Σ(0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 13, 15) using a K-map.

say.en: Minimise F(A, B, C, D) equals Σ(0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 13, 15) using a K-map.
Row AB equals 00 has 1 second in all four cells (0, 1, 3, 2): quad A'B'.
Column CD equals 01 and 11 in rows AB equals 01 and 11 (5, 7, 13, 15): quad BD.
Cells 1, 3, 5, 7 also form a quad A'D, but 1 and 3 are covered by A'B' and 5 and 7 by BD, so it is redundant.
F equals A'B' plus BD.
So the answer is F equals A'B' plus BD.
